composers_checked.name: Quentin, Jean-Baptiste
composers_checked.note: IMSLP files him as 'Quentin I, Jean-Baptiste' (Quentin le jeune); spelt here the usual way. Every recorded chamber work found is kept: Op. 4 Nos 1–3 and Op. 8 Nos 1–3 (Etcetera), Op. 8 No. 4, Op. 10 No. 5, Op. 15 No. 3 (Alpha), Op. 11 No. 4 and the Op. 12 Concerto (Archiv), Op. 10 No. 3 (Electrecord). Op. 11 No. 4 and Op. 10 No. 3 are identified from the recordings' key and scoring against Hoffmann's viol catalogue (the only D-major and E-minor quartets in his prints). Gap check against Wikipedia's work list: all in-scope opuses (4–13, 15–19) are on IMSLP; Opp. 1–3 and 14 are violin sonatas (duos).

composers_checked.name: Caldara, Antonio
composers_checked.note: Op. 1 (10 of 12) and Op. 2 (all 12, complete on Tactus) kept; Op. 1 Nos. 3 and 11 and the Sonata à quattro in B minor have no recording found. Op. 1's separate violoncello part and Op. 2's theorbo/violone part are counted in the continuo (title: 'a tre'). Tactus labels Op. 2 No. 2 'G minor'; IMSLP and Glossa give B-flat. Gap check (IMSLP work info; MusicBrainz work list): the 8 manuscript trio sonatas and the sinfonias have no recording found; cello and violin sonatas are duos; the vocal pages are cantatas with continuo. Not added: the 12 Sinfonie a quattro (oratorio sinfonias for strings; Arcana, cpo, Verso, Arte Sonora), treated as string orchestra like the census does.

note: Both composers are new (not in the violin catalogue or composers.json), so both have authors entries; Quentin is spelt 'Quentin, Jean-Baptiste', not IMSLP's 'Quentin I'. Quentin keys for Op. 8 Nos 1–3 and Op. 10 No. 5 could not be confirmed (neither the recordings nor IMSLP give them), so those titles have no key. Years for Quentin's Opp. 8–15 follow Hoffmann's viol catalogue ('n.d., post 1733'). The Op. 12 Concerto is kept as a one-to-a-part chamber concerto (four partbooks; Ensemble Diderot's recording is one to a part per the Classical Music review). Open: Caldara's 12 Sinfonie a quattro (2 violins, viola, bass; recorded by Ars Antiqua Austria, Arcana 2005) were not added; the owner may treat them like Albinoni's Balletti a cinque.
